title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, is suing the city of Fargo and police detective Lucas Heck for $10m after being falsely charged with bank theft. She was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 while babysitting four children, then spent nearly four months in a Tennessee jail awaiting extradition and about two more months in North Dakota. The charges were dropped after her lawyer showed bank records proving she was in Tennessee at the time of the fraud, and she was released on Christmas Eve.

The lawsuit says Fargo police relied on AI facial recognition that matched her social media photo to a fake ID used by a suspect, without further investigation or probable cause. Lipps says she lost her home, car, and belongings, was denied medications and dentures, and suffered lasting trauma. Fargo officials declined to comment on pending litigation. The case now moves forward in federal court as Lipps seeks accountability and changes to how police use facial recognition technology.
